  3. 5: A Fermat prime (2² + 1), and the only prime ending in 5.
  4. 7: A Mersenne prime (2³ − 1).
  5. 11: The smallest two-digit prime, and a palindrome.
  6. 13: A Fibonacci number that is also prime.
  7. 17: Gauss proved that a regular 17-sided polygon can be drawn with only a compass and
     straightedge.
  8. 19: A centered hexagonal number (1, 7, 19, 37, …).
  9. 23: In a group of 23 people, the chance that two share a birthday is over 50%.
  10. 29: Equals 2² + 3² + 4², the sum of three consecutive squares.
  11. 31: A Mersenne prime (2⁵ − 1).
  12. 37: 37 × 3 = 111.
  13. 41: Euler's polynomial n² + n + 41 gives a prime for every n from 0 to 39.
  14. 43: One of the nine Heegner numbers.
  15. 47: A Lucas number (2, 1, 3, 4, 7, 11, 18, 29, 47, …).
  16. 53: Equals 5 + 7 + 11 + 13 + 17, the sum of five consecutive primes.
  17. 59: A safe prime, because (59 − 1)/2 = 29 is also prime.
  18. 61: Equals 5² + 6², the sum of two consecutive squares.
  19. 67: Also a Heegner number.
  20. 71: The largest prime that divides the order of the Monster group.
  21. 73: In binary it is 1001001, which reads the same both ways.
  22. 79: Reversing its digits gives 97, which is also prime.
  23. 83: A Sophie Germain prime, because 2 × 83 + 1 = 167 is prime.
  24. 89: A Fibonacci prime, and the decimal digits of 1/89 are tied to the Fibonacci sequence.
  25. 97: The largest two-digit prime.
  26. 101: The smallest three-digit prime, and a palindrome.
  27. 103: It and 107 are cousin primes (they differ by 4).
  28. 107: 2¹⁰⁷ − 1 is a Mersenne prime.
  29. 109: It and 107 are twin primes.
  30. 113: The fraction 355/113 matches π to six decimal places.
  31. 127: A Mersenne prime (2⁷ − 1).
  32. 131: Every arrangement of its digits (113, 131, 311) is prime.
  33. 137: The fine-structure constant in physics is about 1/137.
  34. 139: It and 137 are twin primes.
  35. 149: It and 151 are twin primes.
  36. 151: A palindromic prime.
  37. 157: An emirp, because its reversal 751 is also prime.
  38. 163: The largest Heegner number, which makes e^(π√163) extremely close to a whole number.
  39. 167: A safe prime, because (167 − 1)/2 = 83 is prime.
  40. 173: Equals 2² + 13², the sum of two squares.
